A 46-Year Rule Broken, A Nuclear Briefcase on TV & India Locked Out: Inside Shenzhen 2026!

The 2026 APEC Summit in Shenzhen delivered one of the most dramatic geopolitical spectacles in modern history. For the first time ever, Donald Trump, Xi Jinping, and Vladimir Putin sat together inside Kylin Villa for a 90-minute trilateral summit—surrounded by airport protocol shocks, secret bilateral meetings, and an intensifying global tech and oil war.

In this investigative deep dive on Coffee With Sumeet Jain, we unpack everything that actually happened inside and outside the Shenzhen summit—and what it means for India and the world. Why did Xi Jinping break a 46-year Chinese diplomatic rule dating back to 1980 to personally hug Donald Trump on the tarmac, while seating Putin at a side banquet table and greeting Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi with a retired ambassador? What happened inside Trump’s secret 40-minute bilateral meeting with Putin before the three-way talks—and why did all three leaders jointly attack the International Criminal Court while sidestepping ceasefires in Ukraine and Iran?

We also examine the shadow war happening simultaneously outside the conference hall: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s historic military and oilfield pact in Venezuela to neutralize the Strait of Hormuz crisis, Nvidia’s complete halt of Hopper AI chip shipments to China following Jensen Huang’s resignation, frozen data-center loans in Malaysia, Elon Musk’s "T-country" slip from his Shenzhen hotel, and Canadian PM Mark Carney’s controversial tariff deal with Beijing.

Finally, we break down the four massive takeaways for India—from our 35-year exclusion from APEC and the Manila Quad huddle to India's golden opportunity in global AI and semiconductor supply chains.
